title: The Precious Gem (Português)
summary: A nobleman boasts of an uncut diamond worth a province. Birbal shows the court a gem that shines without fading. [PT]
full_text:
A visiting nobleman from Golconda displayed an uncut diamond the size of a fist before Emperor Akbar. 'Your Majesty, this gem is priceless! Kings have waged wars to possess it. It is the greatest treasure in the world!'

Akbar admired the glittering stone, but turned to Birbal: 'Birbal, does our empire possess any gem that surpasses this diamond in value?'

Birbal replied: 'Yes, Sire. In the hut of an honest weaver in the southern quarter of Agra, there resides a gem that surpasses this diamond by a thousand degrees.'

Curious, Akbar accompanied Birbal to the weaver's cottage. They found the weaver, an old man named Kabir, repairing a broken loom while caring for an orphaned child he had taken in from the streets.

Birbal introduced the Emperor and said: 'Kabir, show His Majesty your treasure.'

Kabir smiled humbly: 'My lords, I have no gold or diamonds. I have only this loom, my honest hands, and the blessing of raising this sweet child without asking for a copper coin of charity.'

Returning to the palace, Akbar asked: 'Birbal, where was the gem?'

Birbal replied with profound reverence:

'Sire, the diamond from Golconda is merely cold carbon dug from the earth. A thief can steal it, a hammer can shatter it, and it can bring no joy to a weeping heart.

'But the honesty, selfless charity, and pure contentment of that humble weaver are jewels of character. They cannot be stolen, they never lose their luster, and they illuminate the world with moral beauty. An empire built on diamonds will crumble, but an empire built on the character of honest men shall stand forever.'

Akbar nodded in deep agreement and bestowed a royal grant upon the weaver's orphanage.
